site.name: tablerose
site.summary: tablerose-clone Fictional restaurant reservation platform "Tablerose" multi-page booking flow. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Discovery: hero with 5-field search card (city autocomplete / party / date / time); 5 quick-pill suggestions; 6-card "reserved most this week" trending grid; 4-card editor guides; 3-step "how it works" | | `restaurants.html` | Results: top reservation summary bar with Edit; left filter rail (8 cuisines, 4 price tiers, 6 neighborhoods, 6 features); 10-row results list with photo / name / stars / blurb / tags / per-row time slots (slots within ±30min of search are highlighted, others muted); sort dropdown (relevance / rating / price / distance) | | `restaurant.html` | Detail: split hero (photo / info with stars / dress / hours); 4 tabs (Overview with about, highlights table; Menu with 3 sections; Photos with 9 swatches; Reviews with rating bars + 3 reviews); right-side sticky booking card (date / party / 10 time slots — 30min near target highlighted, 17:00/21:30 disabled for Bella Suora); SVG mini-map; favorite heart toggle |

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tablerose system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the discovery page, testing the search widget and trending links to reach the results page. From there, it will drill into a specific restaurant to test the detail tabs and booking card. Finally, it will walk through the multi-step checkout flow (guest details, payment hold) to the confirmation page, checking form validations and interactive elements along the way.
assumptions: The search widget on index.html routes to restaurants.html or updates state.
Selecting a time slot on restaurants.html or restaurant.html initiates the booking flow to guest.html.
The checkout flow is linear: guest.html -> payment.html -> confirmation.html.
risk_hotspots: Search card inputs (autocomplete, date picker) on index.html
Filter rail and sort dropdown on restaurants.html
Sticky booking card and disabled time slots on restaurant.html
Form validation and dynamic totals/add-ons on payment.html
Small tap targets noted across the navigation and filter lists

phases.title: Discovery & Search
phases.objective: Validate the hero search widget and navigation to search results.
key_checks: Interact with WHERE, PARTY, DATE, and TIME inputs.
Click 'Find tables' to ensure transition to results.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to restaurants.html via search or quick links.

phases.title: Results Filtering & Details
phases.objective: Evaluate the results page filters and restaurant detail view.
key_checks: Toggle various filters (Cuisine, Price, Neighborhood) and Sort dropdown on restaurants.html.
Click a restaurant card or time slot to enter restaurant.html.
Switch between tabs (Overview, Menu, Photos, Reviews) on restaurant.html.
Interact with the right-side sticky booking card.
exit_criteria: Tabs on detail page exercised and a specific time slot selected to start booking.

phases.title: Guest Details Form
phases.objective: Validate the first step of the checkout flow.
key_checks: Fill out standard text inputs (Name, Phone, Email).
exit_criteria: Form completed and navigated to payment.html.

phases.title: Payment & Confirmation
phases.objective: Validate the payment form, add-ons, and success state.
key_checks: Fill out card details and toggle add-ons (Cake, Rose), noting if totals update.
Submit the hold to reach confirmation.html.
Verify 'Modify' or 'Cancel' actions and calendar export buttons on confirmation.
exit_criteria: Reached confirmation.html and verified post-booking actions.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness
phases.objective: Ensure core booking flow is usable on smaller viewports.
key_checks: Check how the search widget collapses on index.html.
Verify the sticky booking card behavior on restaurant.html (does it become a bottom sheet?).
Ensure form inputs on payment.html remain accessible.
exit_criteria: Critical path verified on mobile viewport without major layout breakage.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise search inputs, filters, detail tabs, and all form controls in the booking flow.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the search and checkout flow on mobile to check responsive layouts.

notes: Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets, particularly on mobile viewports.

ux_signals: The 'Sign in' navigation link acts as a dead link; clicking it merely appends a '#' to the URL without triggering a modal, dropdown, or page transition.
The 'Save' favorite button correctly toggles to a solid heart ('♥') when clicked, providing immediate visual feedback.
The 'Save' button has a touch target size of 38x38px, which is slightly below the recommended 44x44px mobile accessibility guideline.
Clicking the 'Reviews' tab successfully updates the main content area to display the review summaries (e.g., 4.7/5 overall rating, category bars) and individual user reviews.
The 'Reviews' tab visually updates to an active state with a distinctive underline, providing clear feedback to the user.
Clicking an 'Editor guide' card successfully navigates to the restaurants search results page.

On the mobile viewport, the filter panel is stacked above the search results, occupying the entire screen. This forces users to scroll past dozens of filter options before they can see any restaurant results.
Mobile layout warnings indicate that the filter checkboxes (13x13px) and several navigation buttons are well below the recommended 44x44px minimum tap target size.

objectives: Verify the functionality and mobile UX of the Party select dropdown on the restaurant detail page.
Verify the navigation from the mobile restaurant detail page to the guest details form.
Verify the functionality of the 'Special request' textarea and its character counter on the mobile viewport.
Verify the functionality of submitting the guest details form on mobile and check if it navigates to the payment page.
Satisfy form validation for the required Phone field on mobile.
Verify if the guest details form successfully submits on mobile after resolving the validation error and navigates to the payment step.
tested_controls: restaurant.html: 1 guest 2 guests 3 guests 4 guests 5 guests 6 guests 7 guests 8 guests
ux_signals: The Party size select dropdown lacks an explicit form label or aria-label, which can impact accessibility for screen readers (missing_input_label warning).
Successfully transitioned to the guest details form (guest.html) on mobile.

The guest details form has a horizontal overflow issue on mobile (page width 450px exceeds 390px viewport), causing fields like 'Last name', 'Email', and the 'Continue' button to be partially cut off and require horizontal scrolling.
Form controls like checkboxes and radio buttons for dietary needs and occasions have small tap targets (13x13px), which is problematic for mobile interaction.
The character counter for the 'Special request' textarea dynamically updates as the user types (e.g., reflecting '21 / 240' after input).

However, due to the horizontal scrolling issue on mobile (page width 450px vs viewport 390px), the character counter situated at the bottom right of the textarea is visually cut off on the right edge of the screen.

Native HTML5 form validation correctly prevented form submission when the 'Continue to hold' button was clicked without filling in the required 'Phone' field. A 'Please fill out this field' tooltip was displayed.

The Phone input accepts standard numbers without auto-formatting them to match its placeholder format, i.e., typing '5035551234' does not automatically convert to '(503) 555-1234'. While functional, auto-formatting could improve readability

objectives: Resolve form validation by filling the required Email field on the mobile viewport.
Verify if the guest details form successfully submits on mobile and navigates to the payment step after all required fields are filled.
Verify if selecting an alternative payment method works properly on the mobile layout and updates the UI accordingly.
Verify that toggling an add-on on the mobile payment page provides appropriate visual feedback and updates.
Verify if the payment form successfully submits on mobile and navigates to the confirmation page.
Verify the functionality of the 'Modify' button on the mobile confirmation page.
tested_controls: payment.html: 🎂 Have the kitchen plate a slice of cake for "Happy Birthday" +$8
ux_signals: The Email input field on the mobile guest details page successfully accepts text. However, severe layout overflow is present (page width 450px exceeds 390px viewport), causing fields on the left (e.g., First name, Phone) to have negative X
Successfully navigated to the payment page after submitting the guest details form on mobile.
On the mobile payment page, there is horizontal overflow (page width 450px exceeds viewport 390px), causing elements like the 'Google Pay' radio button and input fields to bleed off the right edge.
Selecting 'Apple Pay' on mobile successfully hides the credit card input fields and replaces them with an authorization message.

Copy inconsistency: The Apple Pay message says 'authorize the $0 card hold... when you tap Confirm', but the main summary indicates the hold is '$100' and the submission button is labeled 'Hold the table'.
The payment method radio buttons (Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay) and add-on checkboxes have very small tap targets (13x13px), which falls short of mobile usability guidelines (44x44px).

Checking an add-on (e.g., 'Birthday cake plating') on the mobile payment page successfully updates its visual state and dynamically adds the item and price to the reservation summary at the bottom of the screen.
Payment form successfully submits on mobile and navigates to the confirmation page.

objectives: Verify the functionality of the 'Cancel' button on the mobile confirmation page.
ux_signals: Clicking the 'Cancel' button on the mobile confirmation page produces no visible response or state change, revealing it is unimplemented in the current flow.
